Burn It at the Stake! A Designer Set His Sights on a VW Transporter Van and Tried To Make It a Coupe
10 photos
Photo: Rowan Tuttle
Some vehicle designs simply change the game, and the VW Transporter isn’t one of the first to come to mind. However, there are some designers out there that have placed this vehicle in the spotlight and subjected it to the quirks of the depths of their mind.
The VW Transporter is clearly seen as a utilitarian vehicle, one that is used to carry the neighborhood kids to some soccer game, spotted at the heart of countless fleet operations across a wide range of industries, and even subjected to custom work , most often, in the form of a camper that people use to get away from it all. But, it is a workhorse machine, most-often spotted carrying your mail and Amazon packages to your door.
Photo: Volkswagen So, stumbling across a rendering project that explores vehicle design based around the Transporter is something that clearly sparked my interest. It’s called the Transporter Coupe and is the result of a question by its designer Rowan Tuttle: “SUV coupes are a thing. So why not a Transporter with a twist?” A question that very few, if anyone has ever thought of asking.
Maybe some Japanese craftsman or woman has thought of doing so, integrating this sort of look into their wild and transformative van culture. “Vanning” they call it, and some of the designs to come out from this subculture are simply insane. While I’ve never seen a “van coupe,” someone is bound to have thought of it.
Now, all we have to give us an idea of what this design is meant to bring to the table is one or two renderings mixed in with some AI-generated images, the latter standing as a shortcut to visualizing a design that is clearly difficult to image, not to mention putting aside purist design views in order to give rise to such a horrendous monstrosity.
Photo: Volkswagen I mean, I’m not the most car-inclined guy out there, but I do have a couple of favorite brands, with VW being one of them, so whenever is see an exploration around a vehicle they bring to the table, I like to check it out, and in seeing this Transporter Coupe, I can say that I was a bit disgusted; the exploration looks horrible, and it isn’t one that I would ever pay to own, so Tuttle seems to have answered his own question with the design.
I’m curious to read what you have to say about this deep-dive into a side of vehicle design that is rarely, if ever crossed. There’s a comment section below where you can do that.
As for myself, there are a few things I do want to point out, and one of the most obvious is that the ability to accommodate up to nine guests goes out the window, with the slanted and chopped rear of the van removing the necessary headroom for another row of guests. From what I can make out, only up to seven can now be accommodated in the van, maybe even less.
Photo: Rowan Tuttle Not only is the rear of the vehicle reduced, but judging by the size of the side doors, the chassis is also reduced in length. So, any idea that this “Transporter” is to be used in the same way that a real one would goes out the window.
Clearly, converting something like this into a camper van may still be on the menu, but again, it’s bound to be an experience that’s unlike what we’re used to, and the chopped rear is responsible for that once again.
Since space for a bed will be limited inside, so will the ability to integrate a kitchen, dining area, or any other space, so if the Coupe would even make it to market, it’s going to be a no-go for a camper conversion. At best, you’ll be able to toss a bed in there. Maybe these limitations in utility is why we don’t see such a vehicle on the road, or don’t we.
Photo: BMW I’ll be honest and without trying to hurt anyone’s feeling, I may have seen vehicles with a similar rear end before, and there are two that comes to mind. The first is the obvious Tesla Cybertruck, although, it is a bit of an exaggeration, and the second is the BMW X6. I’m going to receive some hate from X6 owners for that last one, but the resemblance is uncanny. Again, just the rear end.
What the concept would look like if it did have the traditional rear end would closely resemble a Scion XB, a discontinued vehicle and brand that some of us weren’t even around when it was “popular.” I won’t lie; I liked it, but I’ve always had a love for quirky cars and vehicles.
However, I can’t say that the Transporter Coupe is a vehicle I like, nor would I ever drop the bucks on one if it ever made it to market. I’m starting ti understand why this sort of look isn’t found in vehicles on the road today.
